design_references.title: Fleet CPG Engine — Phase 1 (Prove the core thesis)
design_references.claim: Overlay build cost (re-extracting facts for only the files a PR touches) must be proportional to diff size, not repo size, or the O(diff)-per-PR architecture is falsified. This is the fact-store-spike measurement of that claim: a minimal tree-sitter-to-Parquet extractor over zod, run full-repo once as a baseline and per-PR (small/medium/large real merged zod PRs) as the overlay.

hypothesis: Overlay build wall time (re-extracting defs/calls facts for only the files changed by a real merged PR) is at least an order of magnitude lower than full-repo build wall time, for real zod PRs of varying diff size (small/medium/large), and does not grow with total repo size (324 files) the way a full rebuild does.
null_hypothesis: Overlay build wall time is within the same order of magnitude as full-repo build wall time, or grows with the PR's position in a large repo rather than with the files it actually touches.
independent_variable: Which real merged zod PR is materialized (three buckets by diff size: small ~2 files/8 lines, medium ~3 files/38 lines, large ~6 files/241 lines), holding the extractor, source repo, and base revision fixed.

environment.network_justification: git clone of zod from github.com (already materialized from fleet-cpg-baseline-zod) and, once, a GitHub REST API call to list recent merged PRs to pick real diff-size buckets. No other endpoints.

variants.name: small
variants.description: Real merged PR #6511 (5ff9566): 2 files, 8 lines changed in packages/zod/src.

variants.name: medium
variants.description: Real merged PR #6488 (212b941): 3 files, 38 lines changed in packages/zod/src.

variants.name: large
variants.description: Real merged PR #5913 (555e5f4): 6 files, 241 lines changed in packages/zod/src.

metrics.acceptance_rule: Accept: median overlay extract_wall_time_ms for every bucket is at least 10x lower than the median full-repo baseline. Reject: any bucket's overlay time approaches the same order of magnitude as the full-repo baseline, or overlay time correlates with total repo file count rather than files/bytes actually touched.

evaluator.rubric: Score on: (1) every bucket's median overlay extract_wall_time_ms is at least an order of magnitude below the full-repo baseline median — the core O(diff) claim; (2) overlay time correlates with files_changed and/or the total size of the touched files, not with lines_changed alone (a large-diff/few-files PR should not necessarily cost more than a small-diff/many-files one) and not with total repo size; (3) defs/calls counts are stable across repetitions of the same bucket on a pinned revision — instability would indicate the extractor itself is nondeterministic; (4) any extraction error is a hard failure, not averaged away.
